title: Charts and maps: Tracking oil and US gas prices amid Iran conflict | CNN Business
text:
Source: CNN

Global oil and US gas prices are persistently high, even though traffic is flowing again in the Strait of Hormuz.Prices eased over the summer after the United States and Iran signed apeace plan to end the warin June, butan escalation in military action in late Augustreversed that decline.

Unblocking the Strait of Hormuz has been helpful, but it’s still incredibly dangerous — andthus expensive. Not only that, but Russian refineries are getting destroyed by Ukrainian drones and Houthi attacks in the Red Sea have disrupted a vital shipping lane.

Gasoline prices havenever been this highat this time of year, according to AAA data.

US gas prices are back above an average $4 a gallon. In June, after the peace plan was signed, gasoline prices dropped below the $4 threshold for the first time since March 30, according to theAAA, but that trajectory has now changed course.

The US national average diesel price is hovering near arecordhigh, according to AAA data.

See the average price of a gallon of gasoline in each state and how it has changed since the beginning of the US-Israeli war with Iran.

Gasoline pricesreached their highest level in more than three years in the early stages of the war with Iran, before dropping off after the June peace plan was signed. Prices have begun to climb again amid renewed hostilities.

— CNN’s Matt Egan and Chris Isidore contributed to this report.
